newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland sells Celuloza shares at PLN 20.5.
newsitem.headline: Poland sells Celuloza shares at PLN 20.5.

text.p: Poland's state treasury at a special bourse session on Tuesday sold all 7.5 million shares offered in paper firm Celuloza Swiecie at 20.5 zlotys, 36.7 percent above its minimum issue price, a treasury adviser said.
"The price was set at 20.5 zlotys...and as far as I know their was a very large reduction of buy orders," Towarzystwo Doradztwa Inwestycyjnego (TDI) deputy president Dariusz Olszewski told Reuters.
The price was near analysts' expectations of about 20 zlotys.
Last week investors registered for the 7.5 million shares, or 15 percent of the firm's equity.
Celuloza Swiecie, Poland's largest paper firm with a net profit of 73 million zlotys on 697.6-million-zloty sales last year, will start regular trade on the Warsaw bourse's main market on Friday.

The treasury ministry indicated on Monday it was negotiating the sale of a 65-percent stake of Celuloza to a consortium led by a subsidiary of South Africa's Mondi, a unit of Anglo-American Corp of South Africa, and expected to close the deal soon after the firm's bourse debut.
